profile.commute: a 1998 Toyota pickup, parks in Lot D

memories.text: Roscoe started howling at four in the morning because the fog horn was running, and he will not be talked out of it no matter how many times it happens.
Decided to move the crane gang shift change from three o'clock to half past three, which pulled about forty minutes of idle time out of the berth window.
The Estrella Meridian is a fourteen thousand TEU box ship and she is the largest thing we have taken on Pier F this year.
Worked a reefer plug shortage and had to shuffle twenty-two containers between rows to get everything powered before the evening gate closed.
My daughter Marisol asked whether ships get lonely, and then asked whether a telescope could see one from our roof, which is the actual thing she wants.
Made contact with a station in Wellington on forty metres at half eight in the evening, which is the furthest I have got on the wire antenna in the back yard.
The pickup rolled over two hundred and sixty thousand miles on the 710 and I pulled onto the shoulder to take a photograph of the odometer.
Took Marisol to the aquarium in Rancho Palos Verdes and she spent forty minutes at the moon jelly tank and eleven seconds at the sharks.
Decided to hold two chassis pools rather than merge them, because the merged pool would have put every empty return on the same three gates.
The gate supervisor Hector told me the new turn time board is showing an average of thirty-eight minutes and that drivers still do not believe it.
I buy cardamom coffee from the cart in Lot D every morning and the man who runs it, Sasan, starts pouring when he sees the truck turn in.
A crane went down on bay nineteen for two and a half hours and we recovered the plan by pulling the last hundred and ten moves to the neighbouring gang.
Decided to give the Estrella Meridian the Thursday night window instead of Friday morning, because Friday's tide and the rail cutoff were going to collide.
Told the terminal manager that the bottleneck is not cranes, it is the empty stack on the east side, and I brought the seven day chart to prove it.
Grilled on the patio while Roscoe sat exactly where the smoke blew and refused to move, and Marisol timed how long he would last, which was nine minutes.
Came in before six because the pilot boat was early, and the fog was so thick on the bridge that I could only see the top two rows of boxes.
There are three vessels working today, two at Pier F and one at Pier G, and only Pier G has the gang I actually trust with the double cycle.
Decided to order Marisol the small refractor for her birthday and to keep it in the garage until then, because she goes through the closet every Sunday.
